metadata.title: Operation Sindoor: Independent public-record investigation
metadata.methods: Source-attributed analysis. An official statement verifies that it was made; it does not independently verify the underlying military assertion.
metadata.limits: Not an exhaustive or completed inquiry. Court records, full chargesheets, licensed satellite images, and original flight-loss forensic evidence have not yet been independently reviewed. No automatic updating configured. Original NIA chargesheet exhibits and commercial satellite pixels remain uninspected. French parliamentary account has been read in original French. Casualty entries are date-stamped reports, not a validated aggregate. Checkpoint 03 assessed Pakistan's claimed 26 targets and the reciprocal counterstrike effects; satellite pixels and grid operations records still unexamined. The legal chapter describes issues and case law but not a court ruling on the conflict.

sources.title: Security Council Press Statement on Terrorist Attack in Jammu and Kashmir
sources.review: Text directly read
sources.note: Confirms at least 26 deaths; condemns attack; calls for accountability; does not identify perpetrators.

sources.title: Statement by Foreign Secretary on decision of Cabinet Committee on Security
sources.review: Official record located via index; source page inaccessible in this research pass
sources.note: Reference anchor for 23 April measures. Detailed legal effects require original-document review.

sources.title: Operation Sindoor: Indian armed forces carried out precision strike at terrorist camps
sources.review: Full release directly read
sources.note: Posted 01:44 IST. Says nine sites targeted, no Pakistani military facilities targeted in opening action.

sources.title: Transcript of Special Briefing on Operation Sindoor, 7 May
sources.publisher: India MEA, published by Consulate General of India Istanbul
sources.review: Full English Foreign Secretary statement directly read
sources.note: Documents Indian attribution, asserted pre-emption and stated objectives. Embedded military-target presentation not reviewed.

sources.title: PIB video recording of 7 May Operation Sindoor press briefing
sources.review: Official video landing page located; video not transcribed frame by frame
sources.note: Firsthand archival video; pending transcription and slide-by-slide verification.

sources.title: Transcript of 7 May diplomatic briefing to ambassadors
sources.review: Web-index full-text excerpt reviewed
sources.note: Pakistan characterizes attacks as violations of sovereignty and asserts civilian harm; independent accounting pending.

sources.title: Demarche to the Indian Chargé d’Affaires
sources.review: Full page indexed
sources.note: Official Pakistan protest concerning 7 May strikes.

sources.title: Recent developments and ceasefire between India and Pakistan
sources.review: Indexed full-text excerpt; source open timed out
sources.note: Pakistan invokes Article 51 and describes Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos.

sources.title: Operation SINDOOR: India's strategic clarity and calculated force
sources.review: Full indexed summary reviewed
sources.note: Retrospective Indian account of strike phases and 10 May DGMO communication; government interpretation of military effects, not independent proof.

sources.title: White House press release compiling 10 May Trump, Vance and Rubio posts
sources.publisher: White House, preserved by American Presidency Project
sources.review: Full release read
sources.note: Confirms US publicly asserted mediation and official contacts; claim of causation still contested.

sources.title: Pakistan's Chinese-made jet brought down two Indian fighter aircraft, US officials say
sources.review: Reuters report and syndication reviewed
sources.note: Two US officials reported; one named Rafale. Anonymous-official reporting is significant evidence, not publicly available wreckage authentication.

sources.title: India says changed tactics worked well in conflict with Pakistan
sources.review: Full Reuters interview coverage directly read
sources.note: CDS Gen. Anil Chauhan acknowledged initial air losses; did not disclose precise count/type. India claimed later tactical adjustment.

sources.title: The Latest: India fires missiles into Pakistani-controlled territory
sources.review: Reporting excerpt reviewed
sources.note: Contemporaneous civilian casualty allegations and aircraft incident reports.

sources.title: How India and Pakistan pulled back from the brink with US-brokered ceasefire
sources.review: Syndicated Reuters investigation read in part
sources.note: Multiple-source reconstruction; includes accounts of foreign contacts and Nur Khan imagery.

sources.title: NIA chargesheets Pakistan-based LeT/TRF and six other accused
sources.review: Official listing and PDF text search preview; full PDF and filed chargesheet not obtained
sources.note: Chargesheet announcement; allegations are not adjudicated findings.

sources.title: NIA supplementary chargesheet names Hafiz Saeed
sources.review: Official listing located; PDF not obtained
sources.note: Announcement refers to alleged individual and leadership responsibility; outcome of court proceedings not established.

sources.title: Operation Sindoor nine reported target sites
sources.review: Original report indexed
sources.note: Details India-given historical camp associations, not independent proof of active military function in May 2025.

sources.title: New satellite images show damage caused to Pakistani bases
sources.review: Report indexed; licensed source imagery not obtained
sources.note: Secondary report of commercial satellite imagery showing physical damage, not aircraft destruction or strategic effects.

sources.title: Clear satellite pictures show damage to Pakistan air bases
sources.review: Report indexed; original image pixels not independently authenticated
sources.note: Describes damage at multiple airbases; follow-up independent image review required.

sources.title: Parliament Digital Library: July 2025 Operation Sindoor proceedings
sources.review: Parliamentary record index located; full debate transcript not read
sources.note: Covers July government accounts; evidence comparison pending.

sources.title: Official account of Operation Mahadev
sources.publisher: Bureau of Police Research and Development (Government of India)
sources.review: Document indexed/excerpts seen; complete PDF not analyzed
sources.note: Government describes forensic ballistics and witness identifications after 28 July encounter.

sources.title: Defence minister denies India bowed to pressure to end Pakistan fighting
sources.review: Reuters report indexed
sources.note: Indian government rejects external pressure as cause of ending operations.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General good offices and de-escalation appeals
sources.review: Full text indexed
sources.note: Secretary-General independently contacted India and Pakistan and offered good offices.

sources.title: Pakistan military response and defensive rationale
sources.review: Same underlying record as S08; retained as cross-reference not counted as independent corroboration
sources.note: DO NOT DOUBLE COUNT with S08.

sources.title: Pakistan National Security Committee statement on Indian measures
sources.review: Public official HTML record directly reviewed
sources.note: Documents rejection of treaty abeyance, reciprocal airspace closure, diplomatic restrictions and trade measures. Statements on legality and attribution are positions, not verified adjudications.

sources.title: Pakistan Foreign Ministry briefing repeating 24 April NSC decisions
sources.review: Public statement reviewed
sources.note: Repeats unilateral-suspension argument; same underlying Pakistan policy, not independent corroboration of S25.

sources.title: PCA press release, award on status of Indus Waters Treaty and interim measures, 31 August 2026
sources.review: Official case notice indexed; host returned HTTP 403 when directly opened, attached decision PDF not independently analyzed
sources.note: Official PCA notice confirms an award on treaty status and an interim-measures order concerning Ratle hydroelectric plant. No assertion of accepted jurisdiction by India.

sources.title: Matters pertaining to the illegally-constituted so-called Court of Arbitration
sources.publisher: India Ministry of External Affairs, Embassy of India Belgrade
sources.review: Original government statement directly read
sources.note: India rejects tribunal's constitution and jurisdiction and says Indus Waters Treaty abeyance remains in force.

sources.title: Air India sees Pakistan airspace ban costing it $600 million over 12 months, seeks aid
sources.review: Reuters full article directly read; reported estimate based on Air India letter, original complete letter not acquired
sources.note: Conditional company estimate for twelve months, not an observed audited 12-month cost. Reuters page displays May 2 UTC update.

sources.title: Air India forms team to drive cost savings, memo shows
sources.review: Contemporaneous current reporting indexed; details independently verified only at news-excerpt level
sources.note: Airline experiencing multiple crises; reported company losses must not be attributed entirely to Indo-Pakistan restrictions.

sources.title: Pakistan official statement of concern about Indus Waters Treaty
sources.review: Original state broadcaster HTML article directly read
sources.note: State broadcaster repeats NSC measures and airspace/trade restrictions. Same governmental source as S25, not independent evidence of substantive claims.

sources.title: PCA case docket, Indus Waters Western Rivers Arbitration
sources.review: Search-index case docket reviewed; direct site may block requests; original 31 August award PDFs not downloaded or fully examined
sources.note: Lists June 2025 competence, August 2025 general interpretation, and August 2026 treaty-status/interim-measures awards.

sources.title: Rajnath Singh Lok Sabha address: politico-military objectives of Operation Sindoor
sources.publisher: India Ministry of Defence / Press Information Bureau
sources.review: Full original PIB parliamentary-remarks report directly read
sources.note: Retrospective account of objectives, claimed more than 100 militant deaths, claimed no important Indian military damage, says operation paused and denies outside pressure. Assertions of outcomes not automatically verified.

sources.title: Rajnath Singh Rajya Sabha address on Operation Sindoor continuation
sources.publisher: India Ministry of Defence / Press Information Bureau
sources.review: Original official PIB parliamentary-remarks account directly read
sources.note: Reaffirms India describes operation as halted, not ended, and restates deterrence and counterterrorism goals. Government statement, not evidence of effects.

sources.title: Pakistan's bid to escalate negated: proportionate response by India
sources.publisher: India Ministry of Defence / Press Information Bureau
sources.review: Complete original PIB HTML release directly read
sources.note: At 14:34 IST India said its defence targets faced drones/missiles during 7–8 May, claimed retaliation against Pakistani air-defence radars and 16 civilian deaths from Pakistani shelling. Operational and casualty effects not independently corroborated here.

sources.title: Press briefing on Operation Sindoor, 7 May
sources.review: State broadcaster HTML report directly read; original briefing footage not transcribed
sources.note: Reports Indian briefing's stated strike window of 01:05 to 01:30 IST on 7 May; this is the officially stated window, not independent weapons-track verification.

sources.title: PIB public photograph album: Operation Sindoor press briefing
sources.review: Official photo-album result located by image search; full license and original image metadata not checked
sources.note: Official historical briefing imagery reference. Do not reproduce in site until publication rights confirmed.

sources.title: At least two Indian jets appear to have crashed during Pakistan strikes, visuals show
sources.review: Original investigation text read; publisher's licensed imagery and original video files not downloaded or separately authenticated in this project
sources.note: Three specialists interpreted wreckage as a Rafale and Mirage 2000; at least two apparent jet losses, with third possible crash site. Report expressly leaves cause and pilot fate unresolved. Rafale markings visible in published analysis; photograph not independently geolocated by authors.

sources.title: Indian strikes on Pakistan damaged six airfields, Post analysis finds
sources.review: Original investigation text read, including method, expert caveats and site summary; licensed underlying imagery not acquired
sources.note: More than two dozen satellite images and videos used; reports damage to three hangars, two runways and two mobile buildings across at least six airfields. Expert cautions facilities not disabled. Pakistani spokesperson acknowledged five base hits and one civilian airport; article reports six PAF deaths, conflicting with prior May 13 five-PAF official count.

sources.title: Audition of French Air and Space Force Chief of Staff General Jérôme Bellanger, 9 July 2025
sources.review: Original publicly published French-language parliamentary transcript directly read, including two relevant passages
sources.note: Bellanger refers expressly to an Indian Rafale having been shot down (un Rafale indien a été abattu); comments that 60–70 Indian and 40–50 Pakistani fighters faced off are his assessment; stated that Indian counterpart informed him India warned Pakistan of imminent raid. These are his statements, not independently examined flight telemetry.

sources.title: Plan to target tourists in Pahalgam was in motion week before attack, NIA chargesheet reporting
sources.review: Original article directly read; attributed chargesheet excerpts and investigative files not independently acquired
sources.note: Describes police/prosecutorial allegations of April 15–16 maps, phones, handler messages and a reported witness. Media on filed prosecution evidence, not separate authentication or conviction.

sources.title: NIA says GoPro related to Pahalgam activated in China, seeks judicial assistance
sources.review: Original media report and court-filing description examined; original signed Letter Rogatory/order not independently acquired
sources.note: Reports Jammu court authorized request for device sales/activation chain in China. Device distribution is no evidence by itself of Chinese state or person complicity.

sources.title: Pakistan says clashes with neighbour India killed more than 50, Reuters 13 May
sources.review: Full Reuters report directly read
sources.note: Reports Pakistan 40 civilians/11 military killed and India at least 16 civilians/5 military killed. These are contemporaneous official numbers as relayed by Reuters, not independently audited identities.

sources.title: 40 civilians, 11 troops martyred in Indian aggression: ISPR
sources.publisher: Associated Press of Pakistan (state news agency)
sources.review: Direct official-state report with attributed military announcement read
sources.note: Pakistan military May 13 statement reports 40 civilians killed/121 injured; 11 military killed/78 injured, including five PAF members. State source not independent verification.

sources.title: Pakistan Foreign Ministry weekly media briefing, 16 May 2025
sources.review: Official transcript indexed and relevant passage read
sources.note: Pakistani spokesperson claims six IAF fighters shot down, showing evolution from May 7 five-aircraft accounts. Substantive tally not established.

sources.title: Reuters did not report Pakistan downed 42 Indian Rafale jets
sources.review: Fact-check original article directly read, including claimed Reuters spoof
sources.note: Identifies fabricated purported Reuters social media screenshot claiming 42 downed Rafales. Provides clear disinformation case; do not conflate with actual Reuters loss reports.

sources.title: French intelligence says Chinese defence attaches spread doubts about Rafale
sources.review: AP reporting and outlet editorial summary read; underlying intelligence report not available publicly for independent replication
sources.note: French intelligence findings described to AP alleging diplomatic influence activity. Distinguish reported intelligence allegation from independently established orchestration.

sources.title: Le Rafale face à la désinformation: lecture stratégique d’un ciblage informationnel
sources.review: Official source located via indexed text; direct full page failed
sources.note: French official analysis of false/manipulated Rafale-loss narratives. Precise publication date not established in this review.

sources.title: Explosions reported after India and Pakistan agree to ceasefire
sources.review: Original Reuters detailed report read
sources.note: Reports firing and explosions observed after 17:00 IST cessation, mutual accusations of violations, and diplomatic/telephone contacts. Observer evidence proves incidents, not responsible party.

sources.title: Armed Forces fulfilled promise, DG ISPR briefing on Pakistan Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos
sources.review: Original state-broadcaster summary of military briefing read
sources.note: Pakistan claimed engaging 26 Indian military targets and effect from cyber operations; not independently proven hit, outage, cyber attribution or casualty damage.

sources.title: Four Days in May: The India-Pakistan Crisis of 2025
sources.review: Specialist analytical study and imagery-evidence caution read
sources.note: Independent synthesis notes imagery confirmation at most claimed Pakistan bases but gaps at several listed locations. Do not count its citations of identical satellite materials as independent original image acquisitions.

sources.title: India claims its strikes inside Pakistan killed over 100 militants
sources.review: Contemporaneous AP account of both sides' military briefings read
sources.note: Indian DGMO says at least 35–40 Pakistan troops killed at LOC and five Indian soldiers killed; Pakistan claimed 40–50 Indian troops killed. Do not treat conflicting claims as verified.

sources.title: India charges Pakistan-based militant groups, six men over Kashmir tourist attack
sources.review: Full Reuters agency dispatch available and read
sources.note: Confirms formal prosecution announcement against six individuals plus group(s), including three deceased during Operation Mahadev and two detained. Chargesheet contents beyond released excerpts not independently reviewed.

sources.title: India Downed Five Pakistani Fighter Jets During Operation Sindoor: Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh
sources.review: State broadcaster original public account of Air Chief's lecture read; raw video/tracking data not independently inspected
sources.note: Air Chief stated five PAF fighters and one larger ELINT/AEW&C aircraft downed; referred to S-400 and claimed electronic tracking. These are dated Indian military assertions.

sources.title: India shot down six Pakistani military aircraft in May, air force chief says
sources.review: Original Reuters report and syndication reviewed
sources.note: Reports A.P. Singh claim of five fighters plus one larger aircraft; Pakistan defence minister expressly rejected and said no Pakistani aircraft was destroyed.

sources.title: IAF chief details Pakistani losses: aircraft taken out on ground, in air
sources.review: Detailed original press-briefing account read
sources.note: Reports October IAF estimate includes aircraft allegedly destroyed on ground and additional shootdowns, not identical category to August six airborne kills; underlying imagery, serial records and electronic tracking have not been independently validated.

sources.title: MEA clarification on Pakistan warning timeline, 17 May 2025
sources.publisher: The Economic Times reporting India's Ministry of External Affairs
sources.review: Published paraphrase of MEA clarification reviewed; full original official release not separately fetched
sources.note: MEA says communication occurred after operation began, not before. French air chief later spoke of prior warning; exact event reference and first minutes still require reconciliation.

sources.title: Prime Minister addressing Lok Sabha special discussion on Operation Sindoor, 29 July 2025
sources.publisher: Prime Minister of India official website
sources.review: Official Prime Minister transcript indexed; relevant portion directly read
sources.note: PM said India's military informed Pakistan within minutes after objectives had been achieved, distinct from French chief's secondhand characterization of advance warning.

sources.title: Pakistan launches Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos, initial contemporary claims
sources.review: Original state broadcaster HTML directly examined
sources.note: Reports Pakistan's own initial claims including destroyed Indian facilities and 70% power-grid cyber disruption. Operational effects not verified.

sources.title: Pakistan launches Bunyan Marsoos, several sites alleged hit
sources.review: Original Pakistani state news article directly examined
sources.note: Early Pakistan report named several Indian bases; says PAF spokesman claimed assets remained safe after strikes on Nur Khan, Murid and Shorkot. Early comments are not a damage survey.

sources.title: Transcript of India's 10 May morning military and diplomatic briefing
sources.publisher: India Ministry of External Affairs, reproduced by GlobalSecurity
sources.review: Full bilingual briefing text accessible on documentary mirror and passages checked against Indian consular official translation; source origin Indian MEA, mirror is not independent confirmation
sources.note: Indian military acknowledged limited damage to equipment/personnel at Udhampur, Pathankot, Adampur and Bhuj; separately rejected Pakistan claims of destruction. Underlying damage unverified.

sources.title: India's Foreign Secretary statement, 10 May morning briefing
sources.review: Original Indian embassy HTML directly read
sources.note: Documents Misri's denial that airfields, Adampur S-400 and critical cyber/power systems were destroyed. Only Foreign Secretary portion, not full military transcript.

sources.title: India DGMO Rajiv Ghai: Pakistan proposed cessation during 15:35 call
sources.review: Indian state broadcaster verbatim on-record remarks directly read
sources.note: Ghai says conversation with Pakistani counterpart at 15:35 IST 10 May followed initial hotline request earlier that morning and took effect 17:00 IST. Pakistan's separate account differs about which side asked for cessation.

sources.title: India and Pakistan agree to cessation after DGMO communications
sources.review: Indian state broadcaster contemporaneous 20:27 IST report read
sources.note: Verifies India's public account of DGMO understanding. Does not establish absence of diplomacy or mediation.

sources.title: DGMOs reaffirm no firing and consider troop reductions
sources.review: Indian state broadcaster reproducing Indian Army May 12 statement read
sources.note: States talks were held evening May 12 and addressed no firing or hostile action and consideration of troop reduction.

sources.title: Indian Army says no expiry date for cessation understanding
sources.review: Indian state broadcaster original report of May 18 army clarification read
sources.note: May 19 publication describes Indian Army May 18 position, no expiry, no DGMO talks scheduled May 18.

sources.title: Pakistan and India ceasefire has no expiry date, officials say
sources.review: Original Pakistan independent press report read
sources.note: Pakistani and Indian officials said truce open-ended despite earlier reporting of May 18 expiry. Quotes anonymous Pakistani diplomat; direct agreement not released.

sources.title: United Nations Charter, Chapter I, Article 2
sources.review: Official English treaty provision directly reviewed in web-index text
sources.note: Article 2(4) prohibition on threat or use of force. Applies to states without settling 2025 self-defence facts.

sources.title: United Nations Charter, Chapter VII, Article 51
sources.review: Official English treaty provision directly reviewed in web-index text
sources.note: Article 51 recognizes self-defence if armed attack occurs and requires report to Security Council. Legal prerequisites contested in 2025.

sources.title: ICRC Customary International Humanitarian Law Rules 1–24
sources.publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross
sources.review: Authoritative ICRC reference rule index directly examined
sources.note: Distinction rules 1,7,8; proportionality rule 14; feasible precautions and target verification rules 15–21. Legal sources not facts about specific strikes.

sources.title: ICRC FAQ: Rules of war and civilian protection
sources.publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross
sources.review: Original ICRC explanation directly read
sources.note: Clarifies distinction, anticipated incidental harm, precautions and presumption of civilian status in doubt.

sources.title: ICJ Armed Activities on the Territory of the Congo, 2005 merits judgment
sources.review: ICJ official case-page summary directly reviewed; complete judgment not parsed paragraph-by-paragraph
sources.note: Uganda's plea of self-defence rejected on particular case facts. Analogical background only, not a dispositive judgment on 2025 hostilities.

sources.title: Indian PIB rejects 70% electricity-grid cyberattack claim
sources.publisher: Akashvani News, Hindi, quoting PIB Fact Check
sources.review: Original government broadcaster Hindi article directly read; English summary manually verified
sources.note: Government fact-check denies a nationwide 70% grid disruption, but official denial alone cannot prove no smaller cyber incident occurred.

sources.title: India denies Pakistan's S-400 destruction claim, AP contemporaneous live report
sources.review: Associated Press contemporaneous dispatch search excerpts read; live-updates page contains multiple items of varying times
sources.note: AP on-record Indian Air Force denial and explicit inability independently to validate Pakistan's S-400 claim.

sources.title: Pakistan's formal conflict narrative Marka-e-Haq, 22 April–10 May
sources.publisher: Associated Press of Pakistan, quoting ISPR
sources.review: Original Pakistani state news report read
sources.note: ISPR's 19-day label incorporates April 22 attack into crisis framing, not evidence 19 days of continuous military combat. Bunyan-ul-Marsoos was announced May 10.

sources.title: India, Pakistan military officials discuss next steps after ceasefire
sources.review: Original contemporary Reuters dispatch synopsis reviewed
sources.note: Reports DGMO follow-up, de-escalation and official accounts. Reuters is a reporter, not a party to hotline.

sources.title: India–Pakistan ceasefire remains shaky
sources.review: Original named author policy commentary directly read
sources.note: Differentiates announced US role, Pakistan acknowledgment of several countries, India bilateral narrative. Analysis not direct participant testimony.

sources.title: Vikram Misri's full statement on reported ceasefire breaches
sources.review: Contemporaneous 23:34 IST published text of Indian official statement directly read
sources.note: India alleges Pakistan breached agreement hours after start; source verifies accusation and dated reporting, not perpetrator attribution.

sources.title: India's official retrospective note claiming 20 percent Pakistani air force infrastructure destroyed
sources.review: Official retrospective press note indexed and relevant claim read; exact publication date should be rechecked against page metadata
sources.note: Claim of almost 20% PAF infrastructure destroyed lacks a published consistent denominator or independent damage inventory in this evidence pass.

timeline.headline: Pahalgam killings
timeline.detail: An armed attack at Pahalgam killed 26 civilians. The UN condemned it three days later.

timeline.headline: India announces punitive bilateral measures
timeline.detail: CCS decisions addressing relations with Pakistan; exact legal implementation of each measure remains a separate line of inquiry.

timeline.headline: Pakistan responds with trade and aviation restrictions
timeline.detail: Pakistan's National Security Committee challenges India's treaty-abeyance declaration, restricts Indian aviation and trade, and reduces diplomatic representation.

timeline.headline: Security Council condemns attack
timeline.detail: Council calls for accountability, without publicly assigning responsibility in this press statement.

timeline.headline: UN offers de-escalation assistance
timeline.detail: Secretary-General held separate calls and offered good offices.

timeline.headline: Air India cost estimate enters public record
timeline.detail: Reuters reports a company forecast of roughly US$600 million in extra costs if the airspace restriction persists for one year. It is not a realized loss figure.

timeline.headline: Operation Sindoor publicly announced
timeline.detail: India states nine sites targeted and says Pakistani military facilities were not targeted in the opening action. A government broadcaster subsequently reported the stated strike window as 01:05–01:30 IST; this remains an official timing assertion.

timeline.headline: Competing state briefings
timeline.detail: India asserts cross-border terror infrastructure and a preventive rationale. Pakistan rejects the justification and alleges civilian strikes.

timeline.headline: First air-engagement loss reports
timeline.detail: Pakistan reports Indian aircraft losses; Reuters subsequently cites US officials. Exact aircraft inventory remains disputed.

timeline.headline: Reuters reports US assessment of fighter losses
timeline.detail: Two US officials tell Reuters Pakistan downed at least two Indian military aircraft; one identifies a Rafale.

timeline.headline: India announces subsequent air-defence strikes and civilian shelling losses
timeline.detail: India says Pakistani drones/missiles targeted its military sites overnight and India struck Pakistani air-defence radars, claiming a Lahore system was neutralized. It reports 16 civilians killed by Pakistani firing by that statement. Each effect/casualty requires independent checking.

timeline.headline: Crisis and strike claims escalate
timeline.detail: Indian and Pakistani official accounts diverge on attacks, interception and damage.

timeline.headline: Independent visual crash evidence released
timeline.detail: Washington Post identifies Rafale- and Mirage 2000-consistent wreckage and an additional unidentified apparent crash site; cause of loss not established from images.

timeline.headline: Further cross-border military attacks
timeline.detail: India describes retaliatory hits on Pakistan military facilities. Pakistan announces Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos and claims self-defence.

timeline.headline: Understanding to cease military action
timeline.detail: India cites DGMO communication. US publicly attributes agreement to diplomatic mediation. The understandings' exact scope and causation are disputed.

timeline.headline: Ceasefire followed by reported firing and explosions
timeline.detail: Reuters witnesses describe resumed fire and explosions, and both states alleged breaches. Responsibility for individual incidents remains disputed.

timeline.headline: Pakistani and Indian accounts diverge on attack effects
timeline.detail: Pakistan state broadcaster claims several Indian bases destroyed and 70% power grid disrupted; India's morning briefing acknowledges limited harm at four IAF stations but denies destruction of S-400 and multiple bases.

timeline.headline: Documented DGMO phone conversation
timeline.detail: Indian Foreign Secretary and DGMO later attribute the contact to the Pakistani DGMO; initiating a call does not settle earlier mediation or who first requested cessation.

timeline.headline: Stated cessation effective time
timeline.detail: Both sides agreed to stop land, air and sea military action; subsequent incidents were reported.

timeline.headline: India alleges evening ceasefire breaches
timeline.detail: Foreign Secretary cites repeat violations after the understanding. The timestamp belongs to published news; each alleged incident time/responsibility must be verified.

timeline.headline: Indian DGMO reports military casualty figures and operational aims
timeline.detail: India says five Indian soldiers died, estimates 35–40 Pakistani soldiers killed at LOC; military assessments remain claims.

timeline.headline: Pakistan describes Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos strikes
timeline.detail: Pakistan's DG ISPR says 26 Indian military targets engaged and claims cyber effects, without independent individual-hit documentation in the release.

timeline.headline: DGMOs discuss maintenance of cessation
timeline.detail: India says the DGMOs discussed not firing or undertaking inimical action, and considering immediate troop-reduction measures.

timeline.headline: Pakistan calls broader crisis Marka-e-Haq
timeline.detail: Pakistan assigns 22 April–10 May to overall nineteen-day crisis and reserves Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos for May 10 counteroperation; not nineteen days of military battles.

timeline.headline: Pakistan issues 40 civilian and 11 military fatalities
timeline.detail: ISPR reports 40 civilians killed/121 injured and 11 service members killed/78 injured. Reuters cites Indian totals of at least 16 civilians and five military personnel killed.

timeline.headline: Satellite review identifies damage at six Pakistani airfields
timeline.detail: Post reports three hangars, two runways and two mobile buildings damaged; Pakistani military spokesperson acknowledges five military bases and one civilian airport struck.

timeline.headline: Pakistan publicly states six Indian fighters were downed
timeline.detail: May 16 number differs from initial Pakistani public reporting of five; not a verified tally.

timeline.headline: India denies forewarning Pakistan before strikes
timeline.detail: MEA says Jaishankar remarks were misrepresented and communication was after launch rather than before; later French military testimony describes advance notification.

timeline.headline: Indian Army says cessation has no expiry date
timeline.detail: Correction addresses reports of automatic May 18 lapse. Pakistani reporting next day also states arrangement open-ended.

timeline.headline: Indian CDS acknowledges initial air losses
timeline.detail: Chauhan tells Reuters there were initial Indian losses, without confirming a number or aircraft types.

timeline.headline: Court of Arbitration issues supplemental competence award
timeline.detail: PCA case docket lists a supplemental competence award, amid India's continuing objections to the tribunal. Original award not independently examined in this edition.

timeline.headline: French intelligence assessment of anti-Rafale influence reported
timeline.detail: AP describes French officials' findings alleging Chinese defence-attache efforts to influence overseas fighter sales.

timeline.headline: French air chief refers to Indian Rafale shot down
timeline.detail: General Jérôme Bellanger acknowledges Indian Rafale loss in French National Assembly testimony and discusses intensive air engagement. Does not identify responsible weapon or release flight telemetry.

timeline.headline: Operation Mahadev announced
timeline.detail: Three alleged attackers killed in an operation; later Indian accounts cite forensic linkage. Underlying ballistic file has not been inspected.

timeline.headline: India's parliamentary debate
timeline.detail: Formal legislative discussion raises operational, security and diplomatic questions.

timeline.headline: Rajnath Singh describes objectives in Lok Sabha
timeline.detail: Minister characterizes overall goal as punishing proxy war, estimates over 100 militants killed, and describes campaign as paused rather than ended. Each outcome claim requires independent audit.

timeline.headline: Defence minister reiterates continued posture in Rajya Sabha
timeline.detail: Government describes the operation as halted, not concluded; declarations about military readiness do not demonstrate further operations.

timeline.headline: Modi says Pakistan notified shortly after objectives were achieved
timeline.detail: Prime Minister describes military-to-military notice within minutes of the opening goals being achieved, in contrast to French air chief's account of planned prior warning.

timeline.headline: Indian air chief alleges six Pakistani aircraft downed
timeline.detail: A.P. Singh asserts five fighter and one larger aircraft losses; Pakistan Defence Minister denies all Pakistani aircraft destruction.

timeline.headline: Indian Air Chief adds ground-strike Pakistani aircraft-loss claims
timeline.detail: A.P. Singh says more aircraft were damaged/destroyed on the ground, a category different from the earlier six airborne losses. Public hull-by-hull independent verification remains absent.

timeline.headline: NIA files principal chargesheet
timeline.detail: LeT/TRF and other accused named; filing does not itself establish guilt.

timeline.time: press report of prior court request
timeline.headline: Judicial assistance sought over Pahalgam GoPro supply chain
timeline.detail: Indian Express reports special court authorized Letter Rogatory seeking information from China about a recovered camera; no conclusion of Chinese state involvement.

timeline.headline: NIA digital-evidence allegations reported
timeline.detail: Indian Express describes April 15–16 location screenshots, alleged phone messages and handler coordination cited in the chargesheet; original digital forensic records remain unavailable here.

timeline.headline: NIA files supplementary chargesheet
timeline.detail: NIA names Hafiz Saeed; independent judicial disposition remains to be checked.

timeline.headline: Indus Waters Treaty tribunal award and Indian rejection
timeline.detail: PCA announces an award on treaty status and Ratle interim measures. India rejects the tribunal's jurisdiction and maintains treaty abeyance.

timeline.headline: Aviation restrictions remain an economic concern
timeline.detail: Reuters describes Pakistan airspace restrictions among several pressures on Air India; aggregate airline losses cannot be attributed to the conflict alone.

claims.claim: Twenty-six people were killed in the 22 April Pahalgam attack.
claims.assessment: UN Security Council statement independently records at least 26 dead; NIA states 25 tourists and one local civilian.

claims.claim: TRF/LeT organized the Pahalgam attack.
claims.assessment: The Indian government states this and NIA chargesheets the organization; a filed charge and official attribution do not substitute for publicly reviewed underlying evidence or judicial findings.

claims.claim: India initially announced nine targeted sites and no Pakistani military targets.
claims.assessment: The verified fact is the public announcement. Actual site identities and damage require separate independent verification.

claims.claim: All nine targets were operational militant facilities destroyed with no civilian harm.
claims.assessment: India's characterizations and Pakistan's contrary civilian-harm accounts remain materially contested; this review has not authenticated all target site imagery.

claims.claim: India suffered some initial air losses.
claims.assessment: India's Chief of Defence Staff subsequently acknowledged initial losses in an on-record interview. Exact number and aircraft models were not given.

claims.claim: Pakistan shot down at least one Indian Rafale.
claims.assessment: Reuters cites a US official specifically identifying a Rafale; this is material evidence, but the underlying battle evidence and serial-specific public authentication remain pending.

claims.claim: Pakistan destroyed five or six Indian fighters as claimed in different statements.
claims.assessment: This research pass found no independently authenticated five- or six-aircraft loss roster. The classification reflects the available evidence, not definitive disproof.

claims.claim: Some Pakistani military facilities sustained observable physical damage.
claims.assessment: Commercial satellite-imagery reporting describes structural and runway damage. The original pixels have not yet been independently reviewed or licensed.

claims.claim: India and Pakistan agreed to stop hostilities on 10 May 2025.
claims.assessment: Both governments and US public communication acknowledge an agreement.

claims.claim: The United States mediated the agreement.
claims.assessment: The US publicly states it mediated. India publicly rejects outside-pressure and mediation narratives. The distinction between diplomatic facilitation and decisive mediation is unresolved.

claims.claim: Pakistan launched Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos in response to Indian strikes.
claims.assessment: Pakistan officially announced and described the operation. The announced results of its strikes are not independently verified here.

claims.claim: NIA chargesheeted LeT/TRF and other defendants in December 2025.
claims.assessment: Official case announcement is documented. No finding of criminal guilt is inferred.

claims.claim: The three people killed in Operation Mahadev were established perpetrators through forensics.
claims.assessment: The Indian government's forensic account is documented; the independently inspected chain of custody and forensic reports are not part of this first pass.

claims.claim: The Pahalgam attack proves a specific advance intelligence warning was ignored.
claims.assessment: A precise pre-attack warning and its handling have not been established in the public documents reviewed. Absence of proof is not proof no warning existed.

claims.claim: The US announced international mediation while India cited DGMO-to-DGMO agreement.
claims.assessment: Both descriptions were publicly made. Their factual accounts of private diplomacy cannot be fully reconciled from announcements alone.

claims.claim: Either side won a total and decisive military victory.
claims.assessment: The record contains both demonstrated activity and important unresolved loss/effect claims, and lacks a single agreed benchmark of military victory.

claims.claim: The use of J-10 aircraft proves Chinese aircraft are generally superior to Rafales.
claims.assessment: Even a validated aircraft loss cannot by itself isolate the causal impact of platforms, tactics, situational awareness, weapons, training, or rules of engagement.

claims.claim: A PCA-administered tribunal issued an award on treaty status and interim measures on 31 August 2026.
claims.assessment: PCA official case docket and 31 August press notice document the award and order. The legal effect and parties' obligations are a separate and contested question.

claims.claim: India accepted the tribunal's 31 August 2026 jurisdiction and award.
claims.assessment: India's dated official statement expressly rejected the award and the tribunal's jurisdiction. This verifies India's position, without deciding whether that legal position is correct.

claims.claim: India's treaty-abeyance announcement conclusively and legally suspended every treaty obligation.
claims.assessment: The disputants' treaty and arbitration-law positions conflict. The tribunal issued an award regarding status; India rejects its jurisdiction. Definitive legal assessment requires full award and treaty analysis.

claims.claim: Air India's US$600 million projected cost was a measured, audited loss already incurred.
claims.assessment: Reuters described a conditional prospective estimate for a 12-month airspace closure, citing Air India's letter. The estimate is not an audited realization and other airline losses have multiple causes.

claims.claim: Pakistan announced airspace, trade and diplomatic restrictions after India's 23 April 2025 measures.
claims.assessment: Pakistan's National Security Committee publicly enumerated these measures on 24 April. Implementation and end dates need separate verification.

claims.claim: India publicly described the initial strikes as limited to nine terrorist locations and not Pakistani military installations.
claims.assessment: Direct May 7 release states scope. Subsequent military-site attacks were described as later responses; this is a statement about announced initial objectives, not verified target characterization.

claims.claim: India's defence minister described broader politico-military goals in Parliament on 28 July 2025.
claims.assessment: Original PIB record attributes to the defence minister a goal of punishing what India called Pakistan's proxy war, rather than occupying territory. This is retrospective language; assessing whether original objectives changed requires comparing contemporaneous documentation.

claims.claim: India's Defence Minister stated that no Indian soldiers were killed during the operation.
claims.assessment: The minister's July 28 wording was that none of India's soldiers suffered casualties 'during the operation'. This verifies the statement, not a complete loss census. An Indian military briefing on May 11 reported five military deaths; definitions of the initial operation versus wider fighting require reconciliation.

claims.claim: India killed more than 100 militants in its nine opening strikes.
claims.assessment: Rajnath Singh presented the figure as an estimate in Lok Sabha; specific independently verified identities, casualty lists and location-level records have not been inspected in this first pass.

claims.claim: India's government described Operation Sindoor as paused, not concluded, in July 2025.
claims.assessment: Primary parliamentary statement in Lok Sabha and subsequent Rajya Sabha briefing confirm official description of suspended military action. Does not demonstrate a renewed combat operation.

claims.claim: India's 7 May briefing placed the initial strike window between 01:05 and 01:30 IST.
claims.assessment: The time range is directly recorded by state broadcaster Akashvani as reported at the official briefing. Precise real-world impact times were not independently reconstructed.

claims.claim: India's 8 May official release reported sixteen civilian deaths from Pakistani fire.
claims.assessment: The official release makes the dated claim, including three women and five children. The individuals and duplicate-free casualty tally were not verified independently.

claims.claim: An air-defence system at Lahore was neutralized by India's 8 May strikes.
claims.assessment: Indian official May 8 release asserted the effect; this first pass has no independently authenticated imagery or post-strike technical report on the system's functional state.

claims.claim: At least one Indian Rafale was lost during the May 2025 confrontation.
claims.assessment: The Washington Post authenticated visual evidence consistent with a Rafale airframe and French air force Chief Bellanger expressly referred to a shot-down Indian Rafale in parliamentary testimony. India's CDS acknowledged initial air losses, but no IAF type-by-type report or independent combat telemetry was reviewed.

claims.claim: A Mirage 2000 appears among the initial Indian aircraft losses.
claims.assessment: Washington Post independently identified Mirage-2000-specific external tank and nearby crash imagery; external tank alone not proof of downing. Original visuals and manufacturer records remain unexamined in this project.

claims.claim: Two Indian fighters had visual crash evidence in early May 2025.
claims.assessment: Washington Post original visual investigation with three experts supported two apparent crashes, while leaving causes unproven. Source analysis not independently repeated by project.

claims.claim: A Pakistani J-10 specifically shot down every reported Indian fighter.
claims.assessment: Reuters cites two US officials for some J-10 involvement, but no independently validated weapon-by-weapon cause attribution exists here for every claimed loss.

claims.claim: Indian strikes physically damaged at least six Pakistani airfields on 10 May.
claims.assessment: Washington Post analyzed more than two dozen satellite frames and aftermath videos and Pakistan's military spokesperson acknowledged hits on five bases and one civilian airport. Original commercial pixels not licensed/inspected by this project.

claims.claim: The damage at the six airfields disabled the Pakistan Air Force.
claims.assessment: Washington Post expert described meaningful but non-devastating damage, and multiple facilities were repairing runway craters by next-day imagery. Physical damage is not equivalent to fleet-level incapacitation.

claims.claim: A Pakistani Saab 2000 airborne early warning aircraft was destroyed in a hangar at Bholari.
claims.assessment: Satellite imagery confirms damage to Bholari hangar, not whether an aircraft was present or destroyed. Washington Post explicitly notes uncertainty.

claims.claim: Pakistan said on 13 May that 40 civilians died and 121 were wounded.
claims.assessment: Verified that Pakistan's military issued these dated figures. Identity-by-identity verification is pending.

claims.claim: Pakistan said on 13 May that 11 service members died and 78 were wounded.
claims.assessment: ISPR figures through APP and Reuters. Five identified PAF deaths cannot establish five aircraft destroyed.

claims.claim: India reported at least five military deaths and sixteen civilian deaths by 13 May 2025.
claims.assessment: Contemporaneous Reuters report attributes figures to India. It does not independently validate names, separate all incidents or prove figures remained final.

claims.claim: A GoPro camera reportedly first activated in China proves Chinese government involvement in Pahalgam.
claims.assessment: A March 2026 judicial assistance request reportedly sought a sales/activation trail, which can reflect ordinary consumer resale. It provides no demonstrated state agency or operational involvement.

claims.claim: NIA says recovered phones contained map records dated 15 and 16 April and communications with an alleged handler.
claims.assessment: Indian Express quotes/profiles NIA chargesheet details and alleged digital traces. Original device extraction and filed exhibits not independently inspected; exact attribution to accused requires proof at trial.

claims.claim: Reuters reported that Pakistan destroyed 42 Rafales.
claims.assessment: Soch Fact Check traced a manipulated purported Reuters screenshot. Real Reuters reporting concerned at least two Indian jets per US sources, not 42 Rafales.

claims.claim: Both sides maintained a complete and uninterrupted cessation immediately after 17:00 IST on 10 May.
claims.assessment: Reuters witnesses reported subsequent artillery/drone/fire incidents and both governments complained of breaches. Incident responsibility remains disputed.

claims.claim: Pakistan publicly said it engaged 26 Indian military targets on 10 May.
claims.assessment: State broadcaster reported the DG ISPR briefing and number; physical effects on 26 targets not independently established.

claims.claim: Pakistan's cyber attacks temporarily disabled critical Indian defence infrastructure.
claims.assessment: Pakistani military spokesperson made a specific cyber-effects claim. Attribution, timestamps, outages and independently authenticated technical indicators not available in this pass.

claims.claim: French officials assessed that Chinese diplomats campaigned against Rafale sales after May 2025.
claims.assessment: AP reviewed French intelligence findings as reported by officials. Authenticity and details of the underlying intelligence cannot be independently replicated here; general coordinated online claims are a distinct question.

claims.claim: French Air Force chief publicly referred to an Indian Rafale having been shot down.
claims.assessment: Original French National Assembly official transcript contains Bellanger's 9 July 2025 words. It proves his stated assessment, not the identity of the specific opponent or missile.

claims.claim: The Indian Air Force chief claimed five Pakistani fighters and one larger military aircraft shot down in May.
claims.assessment: Authenticated as a statement delivered by Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh and reported on 9 August by state broadcaster and Reuters. Underlying electronic tracking and unique aircraft losses were not made public in these sources.

claims.claim: India independently proved six Pakistani aircraft were destroyed in flight.
claims.assessment: Indian air chief cited electronic tracking but this project has not inspected it, a serial-specific inventory, crash imagery or Pakistani admission. Pakistan defence minister denied losses.

claims.claim: The Indian Air Force chief later asserted additional Pakistani aircraft damage/destruction on the ground.
claims.assessment: October 3 press reporting documents broader claims including aircraft alleged destroyed in hangars; it verifies claims, not actual hull damage. Count categories differ from August airborne-interception assertions.

claims.claim: India provided an unambiguous pre-strike warning to Pakistan before launching its opening 7 May action.
claims.assessment: French chief reported an Indian counterpart's pre-raid warning explanation. MEA denied that Pakistan was warned before launch and PM later said notification came within minutes after objectives were achieved. Full DGMO call logs and exact definition of 'launch' are absent.

claims.claim: India's government publicly said it informed Pakistan after the operation started/initial objectives were achieved.
claims.assessment: Official PM statement and reported MEA clarification document Indian position; whether exact chronology matches French official's account is unresolved.

claims.claim: There is an unresolved scope tension between the Defence Minister's July no-soldier-casualties wording and the Indian military's reported five dead in May.
claims.assessment: India's July retrospective wording and May 11 military briefing are independently documented public statements. They may refer to different phases of the crisis; evidence does not show that the minister denied all casualties in the broader 7–10 May fighting. The project must reconstruct what was included under 'Operation Sindoor' in each statement.

claims.claim: Pakistan's DG ISPR publicly stated that Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos engaged 26 Indian targets.
claims.assessment: Verified as Pakistan's 11–12 May announcement, not as an inventory of successful physical hits.

claims.claim: Pakistan successfully destroyed or severely damaged all 26 claimed Indian targets.
claims.assessment: Published independent Stimson imagery assessment saw almost no significant observable Indian facility damage; India reported limited damage at four sites. Absence of observable damage does not prove every missile failed.

claims.claim: India's 10 May morning briefing acknowledged limited personnel/equipment damage at Udhampur, Pathankot, Adampur and Bhuj.
claims.assessment: Original Indian military briefing text preserved in mirror; extent and cause not independently audited. Distinct from claims these bases were destroyed.

claims.claim: An Indian S-400 system at Adampur was destroyed in Pakistan's strikes.
claims.assessment: Pakistani claim and categorical Indian Air Force denial documented. Neither public missile-to-target forensic record nor independently authenticated destruction has been provided; equipment displayed afterward is limited counterevidence, not a unit-wide readiness audit.

claims.claim: Pakistan incapacitated 70 percent of India's electricity grid by cyberattack on 10 May.
claims.assessment: Pakistan's state broadcaster repeated the precise large-impact claim. India's PIB immediately refuted it; no corroborating national outage or grid-system forensic evidence has been found. Smaller cyberattacks remain a separate question.

claims.claim: Pakistan's DGMO communicated with India's DGMO at 15:35 IST on 10 May.
claims.assessment: India's diplomatic and DGMO public accounts give exact time. The raw call recording/transcript has not been released; this does not determine which state first sought cessation.

claims.claim: The May 10 understanding provided cessation effective at 17:00 IST, including land, air and sea military action.
claims.assessment: Indian official announcement and both states' acknowledgment support the effective time. Post-effect incidents are a separate issue.

claims.claim: The cessation understanding expired automatically on 18 May 2025.
claims.assessment: The Indian Army publicly clarified no expiry date; contemporaneous Pakistani reporting also says arrangement open-ended. An earlier reported May 18 extension led to confusion.

claims.claim: Pakistan officially used Marka-e-Haq for the 22 April–10 May crisis and Bunyan-ul-Marsoos for its 10 May operation.
claims.assessment: ISPR account reproduced by state news agency. 19-day overarching crisis label is not evidence of 19 continuous days of direct military fighting.

claims.claim: India's retrospective statement that nearly 20 percent of Pakistan's air force infrastructure was destroyed is independently quantified.
claims.assessment: PIB retrospective assertion lacks a defined denominator, destruction threshold or independently released facility dataset. Independently supported structural damage at six airfields does not equal 20 percent of PAF infrastructure.

claims.claim: Pakistan used Fatah-I and Fatah-II missiles during its May operations.
claims.assessment: Pakistani military officially reported their use and contemporary videos show launches attributed to Pakistan. Original debris and weapon-to-impact chain not independently authenticated by this project.

claims.claim: An Article 51 invocation alone proves that every strike was lawful.
claims.assessment: Article 51 claims require factual and legal assessment of armed attack, necessity and proportionality. Separately, individual attacks remain subject to IHL. Both governments invoking self-defence does not resolve disputes.

claims.claim: Pakistan expressly invoked Article 51 for Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos on 10 May.
claims.assessment: Pakistan official government release states its legal justification. Whether resort to force met applicable legal thresholds remains unresolved.

claims.claim: No public indication exists of any Indian military damage from Pakistan's 10 May operations.
claims.assessment: India itself acknowledged limited equipment/personnel damage at four installations while disputing sweeping Pakistani claims. Not every effect is satellite visible.

claims.claim: The 12 May DGMO follow-up addressed a mutual commitment to avoid renewed military action and consider force reductions.
claims.assessment: Indian Army's dated public account reproduced by Akashvani; actual completed troop withdrawals are not established merely by agreement to consider them.

claims.claim: A building may lawfully be targeted solely because an alleged militant organization historically used an adjacent compound.
claims.assessment: ICRC customary law requires verification that the specific object makes an effective military contribution and its attack yields definite military advantage; proximity alone is insufficient.

claims.claim: The Pakistani DGMO initiated the 10 May hotline contact, so Pakistan must have been the first to propose any cessation.
claims.assessment: Initiating the decisive recorded call is not evidence that no earlier political/military ceasefire overture occurred. Pakistani and Indian narratives on who requested cessation remain contested.

contradictions.title: Aircraft numbers and identities
contradictions.sideA: Pakistan reported multiple Indian fighter losses, initially five and later six in some accounts.
contradictions.sideB: Indian CDS acknowledged initial air losses but offered no count; independent US-official reports support a smaller minimum.
contradictions.required: Individually authenticated wreckage, type and serial evidence, official loss ledgers.

contradictions.title: Nature of the nine targets
contradictions.sideA: India describes all as terrorist facilities.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan states strikes involved civilian sites, including places of worship.
contradictions.required: Facility histories, lawful baseline imagery, source-linked casualty/civilian-use documentation.

contradictions.title: Who caused the cessation?
contradictions.sideA: United States states it mediated through intensive senior-level talks.
contradictions.sideB: India stresses bilateral DGMO communications and denies external pressure as the determining cause.
contradictions.required: Timestamped official call records, consistent contemporaneous accounts, complete negotiator statements.

contradictions.title: Military strike effects
contradictions.sideA: India claimed significant damage to Pakistani military infrastructure.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan acknowledged limited hits and contested broad damage and loss claims.
contradictions.required: Independent historical imagery change detection with non-combat hypotheses tested.

contradictions.title: Perpetrator attribution
contradictions.sideA: India publicly attributed Pahalgam to TRF/LeT on 7 May.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan disputed India's accusations and requested an independent investigation.
contradictions.required: Review filed chargesheet exhibits and any later reasoned judicial rulings.

contradictions.title: Civilian casualty accounting
contradictions.sideA: Pakistan reported civilian deaths from opening Indian strikes.
contradictions.sideB: India asserted precision and restraint and reported civilian deaths due to Pakistani fire.
contradictions.required: Incident-level date, place, person and medical-record reconciliation without duplication.

contradictions.title: Responsibility for escalation
contradictions.sideA: India framed the opening action as pre-emption and deterrence.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan called it unlawful aggression and its own response self-defence.
contradictions.required: Review attack attribution, necessity, proportionality, individual targeting facts, UN Charter standards.

contradictions.title: Indus Waters Treaty status and arbitration jurisdiction
contradictions.sideA: The Court of Arbitration issued an award about treaty status and interim measures on 31 August 2026.
contradictions.sideB: India expressly rejected the tribunal's constitution, jurisdiction and award, maintaining its decision to hold the treaty in abeyance.
contradictions.required: Read full 1960 treaty, the tribunal's competence awards and August 2026 status award, then test India's objections against relevant treaty and international law.

contradictions.title: Initial stated objectives versus retrospective success test
contradictions.sideA: The initial 7 May release described a limited response against nine purported terrorist sites, explicitly excluding Pakistani military sites in its first phase.
contradictions.sideB: The 28 July parliamentary account stated a broader goal of punishing Pakistan for its alleged proxy war and said all politico-military objectives were accomplished.
contradictions.required: Construct dated objective language matrix, distinguish initial action from expanded 7–10 May combat and measure actual disruption and deterrence independently.

contradictions.title: Airframe evidence versus claimed cause of Indian fighter losses
contradictions.sideA: Washington Post photographic analysis supports at least two Indian aircraft crashes but expressly cannot determine whether hostile aircraft or other causes brought them down.
contradictions.sideB: French Air Force chief's public record calls one Indian Rafale shot down; Reuters cites US officials attributing at least two jet losses to Pakistani aircraft.
contradictions.required: Separate existence/type of airframe loss from shootdown mechanism; seek authenticated manufacturer/IAF records and full incident chain, avoiding unsupported weapon attribution.

contradictions.title: Five versus six claimed Indian fighter shootdowns
contradictions.sideA: Pakistani officials initially publicly claimed five Indian aircraft.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesperson asserted six in official 16 May statement.
contradictions.required: Source chronology of individual type-by-type claims and imagery; explain whether the sixth claim represented later incident, reassessment or rhetoric.

contradictions.title: Pakistan Air Force deaths reported as five versus six
contradictions.sideA: ISPR May 13 account disseminated by APP listed five PAF dead within 11 armed forces dead.
contradictions.sideB: Washington Post May 14 report attributed six PAF deaths, five at Bholari and one at Mushaf, to Pakistani military.
contradictions.required: Check full May 14 ISPR original transcript, correction records and location-specific official casualty lists. Do not merge the reported six with the May 13 overall eleven without reconciliation.

contradictions.title: Pakistan base damage versus sustained loss of air capability
contradictions.sideA: India's retrospective account describes successful major degradation of Pakistan airfields and military capability.
contradictions.sideB: Washington Post visual evidence establishes physical damage at six fields, but a cited independent expert regarded effects as meaningful but not disabling.
contradictions.required: Separate structural damage, repair timelines, aircraft losses, sortie generation and long-term sustainment. Do not infer current actionable vulnerabilities.

contradictions.title: Cessation announced versus fire observed afterward
contradictions.sideA: Both governments described a cessation taking effect on 10 May.
contradictions.sideB: Reuters witnesses documented subsequent fire and both governments accused each other of violations.
contradictions.required: Build incident-specific 17:00–midnight time register with independent reports, official allegations and directions to troops, avoiding attribution by assumption.

contradictions.title: Pahalgam phone and camera traces versus foreign-state attribution
contradictions.sideA: Indian prosecution material as reported describes handler messaging and device records pointing to cross-border contacts.
contradictions.sideB: A camera sales/activation link to China does not independently connect any Chinese government body to the attack.
contradictions.required: Obtain court-request return and chain-of-custody documents; distinguish sales geography, device end-user and actual coordination roles.

contradictions.title: Pakistani aircraft losses: Indian August and October claims versus denial
contradictions.sideA: India's IAF chief in August asserted five Pakistani fighters plus one larger aircraft downed; October briefing described additional aircraft losses on the ground.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan's defence minister rejected the August losses entirely and invited independent verification.
contradictions.required: Seek aircraft-unique wreckage or service records, historical ground impact imagery and independent fatality/hull evidence. Reconcile airborne kills separately from hangar ground losses.

contradictions.title: Did India give Pakistan advance warning before 7 May strikes?
contradictions.sideA: France's air chief testified that his Indian counterpart said India had warned Pakistan of an imminent raid to manage escalation.
contradictions.sideB: India's MEA denied advance notice prior to launch; Prime Minister described notice within minutes after first objectives achieved.
contradictions.required: Locate original French officer-contact time, Indian/Pakistani DGMO time-stamped call records and actual distinction between before movement, before impact and after first impact. Do not infer negligence from contradiction alone.

contradictions.title: No soldier casualties during Operation Sindoor versus five Indian soldiers killed in May fighting
contradictions.sideA: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's 28 July parliamentary account said no Indian soldiers suffered casualties 'during the operation'.
contradictions.sideB: Indian DGMO's 11 May joint briefing, reported by AP, said five Indian soldiers were killed during the recent India–Pakistan hostilities.
contradictions.required: Check full original video and literal wording of July minister's speech, May 11 military briefing, and date/event assignment of five fatalities. Do not equate the opening strike mission with the whole confrontation without evidence.

contradictions.title: Pakistan's 26 major target-damage claims versus Indian limited-damage acknowledgment
contradictions.sideA: Pakistan's 11 May DG ISPR briefing claimed 26 targets engaged and major damage to many installations.
contradictions.sideB: India's 10 May original briefing acknowledged limited equipment and personnel damage at four airbases while rejecting claims of broad destruction; independent Stimson study found little observable damage.
contradictions.required: Independently inspect dated imagery and damage claims by facility, separating attempted strikes, acknowledged limited effects and confirmed structural hits.

contradictions.title: Seventy percent grid cyber outage assertion versus absence of corroboration
contradictions.sideA: Pakistan state media on 10 May repeated a claim of 70% of India's electricity grid incapacitated.
contradictions.sideB: Indian PIB fact-check refuted the nationwide claim; no independent national power-grid outage record or technical incident report has been located.
contradictions.required: Locate independent grid-controller statistics and CERT-In alerts for incident window; distinguish distributed denial-of-service, site defacement, local outages and national grid failure.

contradictions.title: Adampur S-400 claimed destroyed versus denial
contradictions.sideA: Pakistani accounts alleged an Indian S-400 missile system was destroyed.
contradictions.sideB: India's foreign secretary and IAF denied destruction; no authenticated wreckage published. May 13 official imagery showed air-defence equipment, but that is not whole-system inspection.
contradictions.required: Determine whether any unique equipment can be matched to source imagery. Avoid publishing current deployment, operating procedures or exact system location.

contradictions.title: May 18 cessation deadline rumor versus open-ended understanding
contradictions.sideA: Some May reporting described a renewed cessation arrangement ending May 18 after Pakistani parliamentary statements.
contradictions.sideB: Indian Army on May 18 said no expiry; Dawn on May 19 cited officials from both sides as saying open-ended.
contradictions.status: Resolved as to public no-expiry position
contradictions.required: Obtain original Pakistani Senate text and DGMO follow-up if legally relevant; do not call open-ended pause a permanent peace treaty.

contradictions.title: Competing Article 51 and cross-border self-defence justifications
contradictions.sideA: India states Pahalgam and threatened further attacks justified limited force against alleged cross-border non-state infrastructure.
contradictions.sideB: Pakistan rejected proof of state support for Pahalgam and expressly asserted self-defence against Indian territorial strikes under Article 51.
contradictions.required: Analyze armed attack threshold, non-state attribution and disputed unable-or-unwilling rule, necessity, proportionality, ICJ practice and time-of-decision evidence for each separate phase.

contradictions.title: Claims of large-scale PAF infrastructure destruction versus measurable historic damage
contradictions.sideA: Indian PIB retrospective material asserted almost 20% of Pakistani air force infrastructure was destroyed.
contradictions.sideB: Published commercial imagery investigations supported physical changes across six airfields but do not provide a denominator or prove fleet-wide operational disabling.
contradictions.required: Define facility inventory and damage denominator, distinguish hits from full facility destruction and find comparable independently documented operational output.

openQuestions.question: What exhibits in NIA's filed chargesheets corroborate organizational attribution and the Operation Mahadev forensic linkage?
openQuestions.next: Obtain full public filings and written court orders; separate claims from findings.

openQuestions.question: Which Indian aircraft were lost on 7 May, with type, number and independently authenticated evidence?
openQuestions.next: Inventory original geolocated wreckage reporting and official admissions.

openQuestions.question: How many civilians died or were injured in strikes and shelling on each side, without double counting?
openQuestions.next: Create event-level casualty dataset from hospital, government and independent incident records.

openQuestions.question: What before/after satellite evidence supports each of the nine initial target claims?
openQuestions.next: Obtain licensed historical imagery and annotate only non-sensitive site-level change.

openQuestions.question: What physical changes occurred at Nur Khan, Murid, Rahim Yar Khan and other publicly named military facilities?
openQuestions.next: Verify original image acquisition dates, registration and alternative causes.

openQuestions.question: What did Operation Bunyan-ul-Marsoos strike, and what independent physical evidence supports Pakistan's claimed effects?
openQuestions.next: Apply symmetrical incident and image-verification method.

openQuestions.question: What role did US diplomacy play, and what formally documented DGMO exchange preceded 17:00 IST cessation?
openQuestions.next: Compare original time-stamped statements and public diplomatic records.

openQuestions.question: Which security warnings and vulnerability findings about Pahalgam existed before 22 April?
openQuestions.next: Review dated public security advisories and accountability proceedings, avoiding present-day vulnerabilities.

openQuestions.question: What quantifiable economic loss can be attributed to airspace and aviation restrictions?
openQuestions.next: Compile airline reports, airspace notices, and audited financial statements.

openQuestions.question: What is the legal effect and contemporary status of the Indus Waters Treaty measures?
openQuestions.next: Compare treaty clauses, official notifications and institutional dispute records through October 2026.

openQuestions.question: Which viral photos and videos were recycled, doctored or miscaptioned during 7–10 May?
openQuestions.next: Build original-post provenance and correction log rather than copying fact-check headlines.

openQuestions.question: What 2026 judicial and institutional developments supersede earlier claims?
openQuestions.next: Find signed orders and NIA releases dated after 6 July 2026; verify not merely case announcements.

openQuestions.question: What is the precise legal significance of the 31 August 2026 Indus Waters arbitration award, given India's express jurisdictional objection?
openQuestions.next: Read full primary award and original treaty, examine constitution/jurisdiction decisions and relevant legal commentary without assuming binding enforcement.

openQuestions.question: What share of Air India's and other airlines' documented 2025-26 costs resulted from the Pakistan airspace restriction?
openQuestions.next: Acquire realized financial data, route-distance changes and airline disclosures; separate conflict-linked costs from other disruptions.

openQuestions.question: Did India's original publicly declared objectives materially change during and after the conflict?
openQuestions.next: Compare 7 May briefings, 10–12 May operational summaries and 28–29 July parliamentary statements; evaluate each goal against independently demonstrated effects.

openQuestions.question: Can a Rafale and Mirage 2000 loss be tied to unique aircraft serials, location and cause without confusing wreckage photos with shootdown proof?
openQuestions.next: Request lawful original imagery, ascertain dates/custody, obtain aircraft-type loss statements; test alternative crash causes.
